76  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

It is to be noticed that careful attention is made to the separation of the sexes: the male and female departments will be kept separate, except in recitation rooms, and no pupils of one department be permitted to associate with those of another.

The 1887-1888 catalog records them in this way, much in the order named, were very clear:

1. The male and female departments will be kept separate, except in recitation rooms, and no pupil of one department shall be permitted to associate with those of another.
2. Calling at private residences of pupils of another department is strictly forbidden, and all persons of any kind will be prohibited by the College authorities.
3. Carousing forbidden, and profane language of any kind will be prohibited.
4. All persons found in the streets or public places at unseasonable hours will be reported to the College authorities.
5. No pupil having the "serenade" or public serenading of any kind will be admitted or permitted.
6. No pupil having the privilege of the upper "house" therefore let it be resolved, that "up-town" serenading should be prohibited.
7. Cards, etc. are forbidden.
8. The standing of each pupil will be kept both as to scholarship and deportment.

As approximately fifty per cent of the students were non-boarders, boarding in private residences near the campus, the enforcement of the strict application in rule six presented some problems. President Halbell made it a point of responsibility himself, and it was his custom to walk about the village in the evening, visiting in the homes of the students. He made occasional calls to see that the students were working at their studies, so the astonished student had had time to run. Contemporaries remembered that President Halbell was wont to arrive unannounced, and in more than one remembered instance, at the home where the young men were visiting the young ladies—not in strict compliance with rules—he would clarify the disturbing matter.
